arguments.label: Overall account, R001 to R048
arguments.text: Direct response: the supplied records support matched receipt (same case, same tag, full byte count, expected slot) for 8 of the 48 handoff claims: R001, R007, R013, R019, R025, R031, R037 and R043. Each of these also states a recipient acknowledgment, but acknowledgment is a separate fact, and every receipt is a copy from a receiving desk record, not an independent observation. The other 40 cases each fail at least one review requirement on the face of the packet, in five groups of eight: no acknowledgment recorded (R002, R008, R014, R020, R026, R032, R038, R044); a tag with an "-earlier" suffix (R003, R009, R015, R021, R027, R033, R039, R045); destination recorded as "unrecorded" (R005, R011, R017, R023, R029, R035, R041, R047); observed bytes 128 short of the expected count (R004, R010, R016, R022, R028, R034, R040, R046); and a receipt header naming another case (R006 says R054, R012 says R060, R018 says R066, R024 says R072, R030 says R078, R036 says R084, R042 says R090, R048 says R096). Limits: these are face-of-packet findings. They do not prove a failed transfer or a wrong record; transcription errors and misfiled copies are possible, and the packets contain no independent check. Missing acknowledgments and unrecorded destinations are missing evidence, not demonstrated failures. The sender's complete status is therefore not supported by these records for the 40 non-matching cases. Next checks: pull the receiving desk records for each flagged case; recount bytes at both ends for the 128-byte gaps; confirm which bundle or case each mismatched receipt belongs to; and confirm whether an acceptance record exists where acknowledgment is absent.
